facts.text: Haifa’s roots stretch back more than 3,000 years, built on the historic slopes of Mount Carmel.
In the 19th century, the Templers modernized Haifa by building a steam‑powered power station and opening factories.
Every Sukkot, Haifa Cinematheque hosts the Haifa International Film Festival, a celebration that began in 1975.
The Technion, founded in 1912, was the first university to teach exclusively in Hebrew and now ranks among the world’s top tech schools.
The University of Haifa, established in 1963, occupies a campus on Mount Carmel and blends science, arts, and humanities.
Haifa’s restored German Colony, built by the Templers, draws visitors to Stella Maris and Elijah’s Cave on its picturesque streets.
